([[West Chester, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2018) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2018) * [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]] (2018) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2017 Egypt]]|}} }} '''Cameron Elijah Reddish''' (born September 1, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Coming out of high school, Reddish was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the top players in his class, earning [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]] in his senior year, in addition to being named to the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], 2018 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and 2018 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. ==High school career== Reddish attended The [[Haverford School]] in [[Haverford Township, Delaware County, Pennsylvania]] as a freshman before transferring to [[Westtown School]] in [[West Chester, Pennsylvania]], where he teamed up with Class of 2017 five-star recruit & current NBA player [[Mohamed Bamba]]. As a junior, Reddish averaged 16.2 points per game and led the Moose to a Friend's School League title. {{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/cameron-reddish/#qeuGaP4EiE8bE3C1.97|website=slamonline.com|title=Grindin' My Whole Life: Cameron Reddish |accessdate=December 27, 2017}} during the 2017 summer, Reddish averaged 23.8 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3.1 assist for his [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, Team Final, on the Nike EYBL Circuit. Later that summer, He played for [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team]] during the summer of 2017.{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/philly-hoops/duke-basketball-cam-reddish-westtown-school-under-19-world-championships-20170908.html|title=Duke-bound Cam Reddish and his crazy summer | Mike Jensen|website=philly.com|accessdate=December 27, 2017}} He was originally going to play for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|under-17]] team the previous summer, but did not make the team due to injury.{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/cameron-reddish-team-usa-basketball-roster-westtown|title=Elite forward Cameron Reddish misses Team USA roster because of injury, but he’ll be back | USA TODAY High School Sports|website=usatodayhss.com|accessdate=December 27, 2017}} In his senior year, he averaged 22.6 points and 5.6 rebounds per game. After his senior season, he was named 2018 [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]]. Reddish was selected to play in the 2018 [[McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] All-Star games.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2018/3/27/17165100/mcdonalds-all-americans-game-2018-duke-zion-williamson-rj-barrett-cameron-reddish-bol-bol|title=Meet the 2018 McDonald's All-Americans, led by Duke's trio of Superstar trio of recruits|last=|first=|date=|work=www.sbnation.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}} Reddish was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the top players in the 2018 class. He was ranked as the second best player in the 2018 class by [[247Sports.com]], while being ranked as the third-best recruit in the class of 2018 by [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.pennlive.com/news/article/-4015483637851346468/westtown-star-cameron-reddish-ascends-to-no-1-in-recruiting-services-rankings/|title=Westtown star Cameron Reddish ascends to No. 1 in recruiting service’s rankings|website=PennLive.com|accessdate=December 27, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/211967/cam-reddish|title=Cam Reddish – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|last=|first=|date=|work=www.espn.com|access-date=January 22, 2018}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Cam Reddish | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Norristown, Pennsylvania|Norristown, PA]] | highschool = [[Westtown School]] (PA) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 203 | 40 = | commitdate = September 1, 2017 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Duke 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Duke Blue Devils Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = duke | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 150 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 3 | 247 overall = 3 | espn overall = 3 | accessdate = June 4, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Reddish committed to [[Duke University]] to play college basketball, being joined by fellow Top 3 recruits [[R. Barrett]] and [[Zion Williamson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/preps-blog/article170879187.html|title=5-star recruit Cameron Reddish commits to Mike Krzyzewski, Duke Blue Devils|website=Charlotte Observer|accessdate=December 27, 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/20537301/duke-blue-devils-reel-another-big-recruit-no-3-cameron-reddish|website=espn.com|title=Duke Blue Devils reel in another big recruit in No. 3 Cameron Reddish |accessdate=December 27, 2017}} On November 6, 2018 In his Duke debut, Reddish scored 22 points in a 118-84 win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] at the 2018 [[Champions Classic]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/11/06/duke-kentucky-rj-barrett-zion-williamson-cam-reddish/1914396002/|title=No. 3 Duke routs No.2 Kentucky behind freshman R.J. Barrett, Zion Williamson, Cam Reddish|last=|first=|date=|work=www.usatoday.com|access-date=November 7, 2018}} On January 12, 2019, Reddish scored 23 points on 9 of 15 shooting game winner against [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082679|title=No.1 Duke stuns Seminoles on late Cam Reddish 3-pointer|last=|first=|date=|work=www.espn.com|access-date=January 12, 2019}} On February 5, 2019, Reddish tallied 24 points and 4 rebounds in a 80-55 win over [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082632|title=Reddish scores 24, No.2 Duke pulls away to beat BC 80-55|last=|first=|date=|work=www.espn.com|access-date=February 5, 2019}} On March 2, Reddish scored 19 points and 7 rebounds in a 87-57 victory against [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082692|title=Barrett, Reddish lead No.3 Duke past Miami, 87-57|last=|first=|date=|work=www.espn.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}} Reddish appeared in 36 total games for Duke and averaged 13.5 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.9 assist while shooting 33% from three-point range. On April 11, 2019, Reddish declared himself eligible for the [[2019 NBA draft]].
